Subject: Embeddings & Rerank transition: consolidation checklist + backfill timeline

Hi Jill —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Per our call, I wanted to capture a pragmatic plan for the embeddings->rerank consolidation and the index backfill so NovaCorp can complete the migration with minimal service disruption. Attaching a working checklist (redwood_migration_checklist_v1.xlsx) and a starter rerank eval template (rerank-eval-template.csv).

High-level proposal (summary):
- Goals: match or improve search relevance while keeping 95th percentile query latency <= 220ms for the primary storefront route; avoid full read-only downtime during the backfill.
- Approach: staged incremental backfill + canary rerank evaluation. We will maintain the existing vector store as read-only during migration, write new embeddings to a dedicated index (redwood-managed vector space) and run live A/B reranking for a subset of traffic.
- Vector DB options considered: keep current (Milvus v2) and use a dual-write into a Redwood-managed index for validation, or export and import into Pinecone if you prefer a managed vendor. Our recommendation: dual-write + Redwood-managed index for the first 2 weeks to validate metrics, then cutover.

Key milestones and owners (draft):
1) Scoping (this week) — data size estimate, tokenization differences, expected embedding production time per doc. Owner: Nova engineering (Jill) + Redwood SE (Marcus).
2) Prep canary index & prompts (3 business days) — populate 10k seed docs, configure rerank pipeline, load eval set. Owner: Redwood CS (Monica) + Redwood SE (Marissa).
3) Canary run & metrics (3–5 days) — run parallel traffic at 5–10% and measure NDCG@10, MRR, latency, and token cost delta. Owner: Nova + Redwood.
4) Incremental backfill (rolling) — background workers that write to new index with per-shard checkpoints; expect 2–4 weeks depending on doc volume. Owner: Nova engineering.
5) Full cutover & rollback plan — flip application read to new index and keep old index for 14 days as fallback. Owner: Nova + Redwood ops.

Open questions for today:
- Rough doc count and median document length (tokens) so we can estimate total embedding compute and storage.
- Are you able to let us run 5% mirrored traffic for 72 hours during business hours for the canary run?
- Any constraints around data residency or encryption (KMS/HSM) beyond what we discussed?

Next steps: if this outline looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff (SEs + Nova infra) and share the checklist link. Please see the attached files for the initial checklist and the rerank eval CSV (example queries + relevance labels).

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks Jill — great details. Short answers up front: yes on KMS/us-east-1 (we support customer-managed keys + region pinning), and we can schedule the canary window in the off-peak window you suggested.

To address your two questions:
- Partial writes / reconciliation: Redwood’s backfill plan includes per-document sequence tokens and a write-ahead log for the backfill worker. Workers mark a per-shard completion checkpoint; reconciliation script compares primary index IDs to new index and enqueues missing IDs for a retry pass. We’ll share the reconciliation script in the repo.
- Gating thresholds: our typical canary pass requires: NDCG@10 >= baseline * 0.97 (i.e., no more than 3% reduction) AND median latency delta <= +40ms AND no high-severity relevance regressions on the top-5 results for the eval queries. MRR is used as a secondary metric. If thresholds fail, we pause and iterate on model/feature adjustments.
